title: BrightCart Labs — Legal & Procurement Onboarding Preflight
summary: High-level preflight between Redwood AE/SE and BrightCart procurement/security/legal to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/egress, and pricing path. Customer flagged two blockers: data residency for EU customers and a required KMS/HSM integration for privileged keys. Agreed next steps: send redline-friendly MSA, security attachments, pricing scenarios, and schedule technical deep-dive for private deployment networking.
action_items: Marissa Chen | Share MSA marked-up template and DPA appendix link | 2025-04-08
Diego Rios | Set up technical deep-dive for private VPC networking and KMS flow, include latency/throughput notes | 2025-04-11
Priya Rao | Send BrightCart's required accreditation checklist and KMS requirements doc to Redwood | 2025-04-06
Aaron Cole | Provide target traffic profile and retention policy for pilot (sample requests per minute, seq len) | 2025-04-07
next_steps: Redwood to email MSA/DPA redlines + security deck (SOC2, ISO) and KMS integration notes
Schedule private deployment network deep-dive (SE-led) week of Apr 14
Procurement to circulate Redwood pricing scenarios to Finance and return questions by Apr 10
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rios (Redwood SE), Hannah Patel (Redwood Solutions), Liam O'Neill (BrightCart Procurement), Priya Rao (BrightCart Security), Aaron Cole (BrightCart Platform), Nora Kim (BrightCart Legal)

Summary (auto): preflight to align legal and technical blockers before procurement gate.

[00:00] Marissa Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick round-robin, i'm marissa, redwood account owner, and i'll hand to diego for the tech bits later.
[00:09] Liam O'Neill: hi, liam here, vp procurement at brightcart, quick agenda — legal redlines, pricing path, and security must-haves from priy a.
[00:18] Priya Rao: hi, yeah thanks, i'm priya security lead, a few non-negotiables: customer-managed keys or HSM KMS option, audit logs retained for 1 year, and EU data residency for eu shoppers.
[00:30] Marissa Chen: got it, thanks, those are common. quick clarification on the keying — are you expecting our private deployment option or do you need a hosted offering with customer key control via bring-your-own-kms?
[00:45] Priya Rao: ideally customer-managed keys in our VPC, like BYOK to our HSM. Hosted with BYOK is acceptable if keys never leave HSM, but procurement prefers private.
[00:58] Diego Rios: (SE) yeah technically we support both — private gives direct KMS integration, hosted can do KMS via external key encryption if requirements allow. there is some egress nuance, though, egress fees if traffic leaves eu region.
[01:12] Nora Kim: quick legal note — on the MSA DPA, our counsel flagged the standard limitation of liability language and the data deletion timing; we need clear SLA remediation windows.
[01:24] Marissa Chen: understood, we can identify remediation SLAs and a canary for rollbacks; our standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted, dedicated can go to 99.95 with reserved capacity — but we can discuss credits.
[01:39] Liam O'Neill: pricing, is that per-token still? our unit economics team keeps asking about per-token vs per-request for embeddings.
[01:46] Hannah Patel: yes, hosted API is per-token; embeddings are per-vector unit. dedicated has committed throughput pricing and predictable monthly fee plus usage overage. we'll share a pricing spreadsheet with scenarios.
[02:05] Aaron Cole: our main workload is product search rerank and chat assistant on mobile, typical sequence length about 256 tokens, peak TPS around 60 req/s, avg 20 — does that change recommended footprint?
[02:18] Diego Rios: 60 rps peak is substantial, for pure hosted you might see variable latency at peak; for strict SLOs we recommend either dedicated pools or a private deployment with autoscaling. also look at our batching and prefix cache to reduce cost.
[02:33] Priya Rao: can you confirm how long kv cache persists and whether it's exportable? we have concerns about persistent stored context for EU residents.
[02:44] Diego Rios: kv cache is in-memory per instance, not written to disk; we can configure retention windows and shard by tenant, but i'll follow up with exact guarantees.
[02:56] Nora Kim: about the DPA — we have a requirement to list sub processors and to allow 30 day notification for changes, is that in your DPA?
[03:06] Marissa Chen: our standard DPA lists sub-processors and we can include a 30-day notice; i'll flag the legal team to prep that appendix.
[03:15] Liam O'Neill: procurement process — our buying committee wants the MSA with redlines, security questionnaire, and a 3-month pilot pricing scenario. can you support a pilot with limited commit?
[03:25] Marissa Chen: absolutely, we run pilots often; we'll put together a limited pilot SKU for dedicated/reserved and a hosted fallback; also we can set an SLA target for the trial.
[03:35] Priya Rao: SOC 2 attestation — we need the report and evidence of iso alignment.
[03:40] Hannah Patel: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 infra; i'll attach the latest audit report and a summary of controls in the security deck.
[03:49] Aaron Cole: on private deployment networking, our infra team requires a peering pattern and route map, plus support for mutual TLS and SAML SSO.
[03:59] Diego Rios: for VPC private we do VPN or AWS PrivateLink, support mTLS, and SAML SSO is supported via standard identity providers; i'll prepare a diagram and checklist.
[04:12] Nora Kim: about indemnity and export controls — we operate in multiple jurisdictions. we need export control clause tailored and a list of certified data centers for regions.
[04:23] Marissa Chen: export controls set in addendum — we can provide region-specific data center lists and confirm egress geography.
[04:30] Liam O'Neill: timeline — if procurement OKs, we want pilot start mid-may. is that feasible?
[04:36] Marissa Chen: yes, mid-may pilot start is doable assuming legal sign-off by early May.
[04:42] Priya Rao: one more thing, how do you handle key rotation and emergency key revocation?
[04:49] Diego Rios: key rotation is customer-driven when BYOK, we support rotation APIs and immediate revocation; in hosted we have a key versioning layer — will document specifics.
[04:59] Hannah Patel: i'll also include our recommended rotation cadence and an incident runbook excerpt.
[05:05] Aaron Cole: ok good. can you also confirm latency SLO per region, e.g., eu-west 1 p95?
[05:11] Diego Rios: p95 numbers depend on model and sequence len, but we can provide model profiles — for your 256 tokens we'd expect p95 sub-300ms on dedicated in region, hosted varies. we'll include a benchmark sheet.
[05:25] Nora Kim: legal wants a clause for forensic audits and 30 day support for data subject requests — can you accommodate?
[05:32] Marissa Chen: yes, DSAR support is standard; forensic assistance is available under enterprise agreements — we'll mark in MSA.
[05:38] Liam O'Neill: procurement needs to know billing path for egress fees — is egress charged per-GB plus sliding scale?
[05:45] Hannah Patel: egress is region dependent; for private deployments egress is minimal if within VPC, for hosted there may be per-GB charges; we'll put concrete numbers in the pricing scenarios.
[05:58] Priya Rao: anything else from red team? we also ask for vulnerability disclosure program details and SLA for patching critical CVEs.
[06:08] Diego Rios: we have a vulnerability disclosure and patching windows; critical CVEs patched within X days typically — we'll provide exact SLAs.
[06:18] Marissa Chen: okay let's summarize next steps and owners.
[06:22] Marissa Chen: action recap: i'll send MSA + DPA redlines and security deck; diego will schedule network deep-dive and deliver KMS flow doc; hannah will share SOC2 and pricing spreadsheet; brightcart to send traffic profile and legal redline notes.
[06:40] Liam O'Neill: sounds good, we'll aim to get initial redlines back by Apr 10 and procurement will review pricing by Apr 12.
[06:48] Marissa Chen: perfect thank you all, we'll follow up by email with attachments and proposed deep-dive slots.
[06:55] (meeting ends)
notes: Transcript has occasional mis-hearings: 'key V cache' for kv cache, 'per token' sometimes transcribed as 'per-ton', and speaker overlap noted around 03:35-03:40. Customer emphasis on BYOK and EU residency — potential procurement blocker until private/KMS path confirmed.
